title: Reactive Programming Patterns
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of reactive programming patterns and name the relevant Angular concepts.
Apply at least one syllabus item from this lesson in a focused Angular example.
Verify expected behavior and identify one compatibility, failure or trust-boundary limitation.

content.intro: This lesson focuses on reactive programming patterns inside RxJS and Asynchronous Programming. Begin with the syllabus anchor “Event-driven workflows”, name the data or UI behavior involved, and then verify the result with a focused example. The goal is to make one clear engineering decision rather than memorize an isolated API.
content.why_it_matters: Network and asynchronous failures are normal. A reliable application models loading, success, empty and error states instead of assuming every operation succeeds.

content_blocks.title: Inspectable example: Reactive Programming Patterns
content_blocks.code:
import { of, map } from 'rxjs';

of(1, 2, 3).pipe(map(value => value * 2)).subscribe(value => console.log(value));
content_blocks.expected_output: Console output: 2, then 4, then 6. Observables can model streams; manage long-lived subscriptions and cancellation intentionally.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a snippet without checking its surrounding context.
common_mistakes.why: Angular examples can depend on imports, providers, template context or a particular framework version.
common_mistakes.fix: Use the run instructions and validate against the exact generated workspace.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating an attractive UI result as proof of correctness.
common_mistakes.why: Accessibility, boundary cases, failures and server-side rules may not be visible in the happy path.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a focused assertion and test at least one realistic failure state.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming client code guarantees authorization or validates all external data.
common_mistakes.why: Browser code is controlled by the client and can receive unexpected network responses.
common_mistakes.fix: Validate external values and enforce protected business rules on the backend.
